collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder advises a teen choosing a trade to become a healer: become a healer, or become a builder.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is old enough to start learning a trade, and (subject.he/she) can't choose between the healers and the builders. (subject.He/she) asks (friend) for advice. (friend) thinks carefully and says, "You have steady hands and a kind heart. I think you'd make a fine healer."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes to the healers. (subject.He/she) likes it. Some days (subject.he/she) loves it. Some days (subject.he/she) wishes (subject.he/she) were up on a roof in the sunshine instead. (subject.He/she) never quite knows if (friend) was right. Maybe (subject.he/she) would have been just as happy building. Maybe not. (subject.He/she) is a good healer, and that's something.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Thank you," says (subject). "But I think I want to build." (friend) nods, not at all offended. "Steady hands are good for building too." (subject) becomes a builder. Years later, (subject.he/she) still helps the healers sometimes when an extra pair of hands is needed. (subject.He/she) never regrets the choice. (subject.He/she) never feels (subject.he/she) ignored (friend) either. (subject.He/she) just listened, and then chose.
